reasons: upper mass remains calm and distinct from the ground relation
fits the neighborhood active-edge + public-space hierarchy better than a pure box

rationale: Only one candidate is visible, so the portfolio cannot pass a 20-option diversity audit. The single mass does show a decent neighborhood-building direction: compact, capacity-aware, with a legible carved void and a restrained upper body. But as a portfolio it has no breadth, no dominant-family control metric, and no demonstrated range of program-specific spatial languages. For the next iteration, prioritize clear form-section diversity while preserving the active street edge and a usable public void/terrace relationship.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: single compact oblique block with one carved open-court/roof notch; read as one repeated block family if extended

required_next_relations: Introduce at least 9 additional materially different spatial families beyond this carved block: e.g. slot void, stepped terrace, bent bar, twin-volume court, bridge/podium, split mass, corner pinch, sawtooth section, stacked plinth, porous cluster.
Keep the ground edge explicitly active on the west access side in every new family.
Make at least one family where the public void is a true usable court or terrace, not just a notch.
Vary section logic as much as silhouette: low-rise plinth + calm upper bar, offset volumes, lifted piece, recessed ground, and a more horizontal mixed-use section are all preferable.
Avoid cloning the same prismatic block with only roof-angle changes; roof variation alone will not count as a new family.
